title: What makes something fair?
summary: Steelman both sides of what fair really means, then debate whether fair means everyone gets the same.

steps.title: Fair as equal, fair as needed
steps.body:
Fair can mean two different things, and people often talk past each other because they each mean a different one. Fair as equal: everyone gets exactly the same amount, no matter what. Fair as needed: everyone gets what actually helps them, which might not be the same amount for everyone.

Think about splitting one pizza between two people: one who has not eaten all day and is starving, and one who just finished a big lunch and is only a little hungry. Equal would cut the pizza exactly in half. Needed might give the hungrier person more, since an equal split leaves one person still starving and the other person stuffed with food they did not need.

Or think about a row of kids trying to see over a fence at a game. If every kid stands on a box of the exact same height, that is fair as equal, but a shorter kid still cannot see over the fence while a taller kid could already see without any box at all. A box sized to each kid, so everyone's eyes end up level with the top of the fence, is fair as needed, even though the boxes are not the same size.

Steelman first, same rule as every debate this season: before you argue your own side, say the strongest version of the other side's point, in your own words, not a weak one. Someone arguing fair means equal might say that giving people different amounts opens the door to favorites and unfair guesses about who really needs more. Someone arguing fair means needed might say that treating unequal situations identically does not erase the difference between them, it just ignores it.

This week's skill is reflection: after the debate ends, look back at what you actually said, not what you meant to say, and name one thing you would change if you argued it again. A good reflection names the moment, not just a feeling: which point landed, which one you fumbled, and what you would say instead.

Three rounds, and the motion is the question itself: fair means everyone gets the same.

steps.title: Record it
steps.prompt: Record part of the debate, or record yourself afterward reflecting on one moment you would argue differently and why.
